Dijkstra finalises a node once popped; a later negative edge could still make it shorter, so results break.

options: Parallel execution of Python bytecode across threads
quiz.explain: The GIL lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time, so CPU-bound threads do not run in parallel.
fork() duplicates the calling process; the parent and the new child continue from the same point.

practice.title: /enrich fan-out

quiz.prompt: In TaskGroup, if one task raises:
options: Remaining tasks are cancelled and errors raised together
quiz.explain: TaskGroup cancels the other tasks when one fails and raises the failures together as an ExceptionGroup.
A Semaphore(5) lets at most five coroutines inside `async with sem:` at once; others wait.

quiz.prompt: Calling a blocking SDK inside an `async def` endpoint without to_thread:
options: Stalls every request on that worker
quiz.explain: A blocking call never yields to the event loop, so every other request on that worker waits.

quiz.prompt: A per-request DB session should be:
